data.text: Claude just arrived and is getting ready to work.

data.title: Planning the build
data.oneLiner: Before writing code, the agent reads what exists and makes a plan, like a recipe or a protocol.

analogy.office: A team meeting at the whiteboard before work starts.
analogy.lab: Writing your protocol before you touch a pipette.
analogy.kitchen: Reading the whole recipe before you turn on the stove.

data.text: Claude is reading App.tsx in the Microscope room to understand how what the user sees (the frontend) works right now.

data.title: What is a frontend?
data.oneLiner: The frontend is everything the user sees and clicks: pages, buttons, colors.

analogy.office: The shop window and the front desk.
analogy.lab: The microscope image you actually look at, not the machinery inside.
analogy.kitchen: The plated dish the guest sees on the table.

data.text: Claude made a small change in the Sample intake. This part of the app is about how programs talk to each other (the API).

data.title: What is an API?
data.oneLiner: An API is a set of agreed requests one program can send another, and the answers it gets back.

analogy.office: The mail room: you send a request in the right format and get a reply.
analogy.lab: The sample intake window: drop off a labeled sample, get results back.
analogy.kitchen: The order window: a ticket goes in, a finished dish comes out.

data.text: Claude is running the tests: automatic checks that the app still does what it should.

data.title: Why tests?
data.oneLiner: Tests are small automatic checks that the code still does what it should after every change.

analogy.office: Quality check before a product ships.
analogy.lab: Running a control alongside every experiment.
analogy.kitchen: Tasting the soup before it leaves the kitchen.
